blockingLoop.evidence: Four consecutive turns tell her to run a spin/drain programme and listen for 'humming' at the bottom front, plus repeating 'We can look for the model number on the back of the machine later' despite her twice saying she cannot distinguish humming and the pump 'just runs for a bit then stops'.

rationale: The assistant fixated on a drain/pump blockage framing and repeated the same 'run spin, listen for humming' instruction four times, never adapting when the customer said she couldn't interpret the sound and that the display freezes with no odd noises. It ignored strong clues (display freezes, intermittent stalls, most washes complete, filter already cleaned twice) that point toward pressure switch/pump/board uncertainty, never asked about flashing-light patterns or codes, and never recommended an engineer for an out-of-warranty 6-year-old intermittent fault. It did not invent evidence or push a part, and gave no unsafe instruction, but the conversation made essentially no diagnostic progress and would leave a UK homeowner frustrated.
